childRuns.label: Result Analyst
childRuns.summary:
Verdict: weak_support
Key finding: Mean accuracy lift is 1.9% and mean macro-F1 lift is 1.2%, but no statistical test or confidence interval is present.
Evidence: Baseline-A mean accuracy 84.3% | SciForgeNet mean accuracy 86.2% | 3 seeds available
Recommendation: Add confidence intervals and a paired or bootstrap significance test before using "significantly outperforms".

childRuns.label: Baseline Critic
childRuns.summary:
Verdict: not_fair_yet
Key finding: The method and baseline use different preprocessing, image size, and augmentation settings.
Evidence: Baseline preprocessing standard_v1, image size 224 | Method preprocessing augmented_v2, image size 256 | Method augmentation random_crop,color_jitter
Recommendation: Re-run Baseline-A under the same preprocessing and image-size policy, or narrow the claim to this exact setup.

childRuns.label: Reproducibility Auditor
childRuns.summary:
Verdict: partially_reproducible
Key finding: Seeds and logs exist, but the environment is under-specified.
Evidence: Recorded seeds: 11, 22, 33 | CUDA: not recorded | Requirements lock: missing
Recommendation: Add a locked environment file and record CUDA/library versions before treating this as manuscript-grade evidence.

childRuns.label: Data Risk Auditor
childRuns.summary:
Verdict: high_risk
Key finding: The dataset summary reports train-test duplicate patient IDs and a large positive-rate shift.
Evidence: Train-test duplicate patient IDs: 7 | Train positive rate 18.0% | Test positive rate 9.0%
Recommendation: Remove overlapping patients, regenerate splits, and report class-balanced metrics after the fix.

childRuns.label: Claim Critic
childRuns.summary:
Verdict: not_ready
Key finding: The current evidence supports "higher observed accuracy in this run package", not "significantly outperforms".
Evidence: Observed accuracy lift 1.9% | No significance test | Fairness and data-risk agents found blocking issues
Recommendation: Downgrade the claim or complete the blocking follow-up experiments before writing it into the paper.
